dream: The sharp strip became a fish, its edge swimming through the air while the card hummed like a drum. I pressed the round rock down on the wide anchor, but the anchor slid away onto my own shoulder. The slip drifted, trailing a string of cool dust that felt like cold water. I woke the bush by scratching its leaf until it uncurled into a fan. Then the heavy lid fell from the ceiling, crushing the dot into a flat stain. I lay still under the Warm Blanket, waiting for the air to decide if it wanted to be thick or thin.
